words.gloss: the lord of the maritime tract

literal: Without cherishing, even if he does only what he desires, without seeing the lord of the maritime tract, they do not rest, the eyes.
translation: Even if my lord acts only as he pleases without cherishing me, my eyes will not rest unless they see him.
modern: தலைவன் என்னை மதிக்காமல் தன் விருப்பப்படியே செய்தாலும், அவனைக் காணாமல் என் கண்கள் அமைதியடையா.
explanation: In this verse, the heroine describes her uncontrollable longing to her companion. Even when her husband, the lord of the maritime tract (koṇkaṉ), neglects her feelings (pēṇātu) and acts solely according to his own desires (peṭpavē), she cannot remain angry. Her eyes (kaṇ) refuse to find rest or be satisfied (amaiyala) unless they can behold him (kāṇātu). The word 'amaiyala' combines 'amai' (to rest or be content) and the negative plural suffix 'ala', perfectly capturing how her eyes rebel against her own resolve to stay away.
